nodes.summary: One step of the Wold decomposition: every vector splits as a wandering vector plus a vector in the range.
nodes.title: One-step Wold splitting into wandering vector plus range

nodes.summary: Finite Wold decomposition: every vector is a finite sum of pushed-forward wandering vectors plus a remainder in the range of `V ^ n`. The wandering coefficients vanish at and beyond `n`.
nodes.title: Finite Wold decomposition

nodes.summary: Pulling inner products back along powers of an isometry.
nodes.title: Powers of an isometry preserve inner products
Orthogonality of pushed-forward wandering vectors, symmetric form

nodes.summary: A wandering vector, pushed forward `k` times, is orthogonal to any vector pushed forward strictly more times.
nodes.title: Orthogonality of pushed-forward wandering vectors

nodes.summary: The residual subspace is orthogonal to every pushed-forward wandering vector: the wandering part and the residual part of Wold's decomposition are orthogonal.
nodes.title: Residual subspace is orthogonal to the wandering part

nodes.summary: The restriction of an isometry to its residual subspace preserves inner products.
nodes.title: Isometry restricted to the residual subspace preserves inner products

nodes.summary: The ambient space splits as the wandering subspace plus the range.
nodes.title: Wandering subspace and range are complementary

nodes.summary: The isometry maps its residual subspace into itself.
nodes.title: An isometry maps its residual subspace into itself

nodes.summary: A positive power of an isometry lands in the range of the isometry.
nodes.title: Positive powers of an isometry land in its range

nodes.summary: The residual subspace of an isometry: vectors in the range of every power of `V`.
nodes.title: Residual subspace of an isometry

nodes.summary: The restriction of an isometry to its residual subspace is bijective.
nodes.title: Isometry restricted to the residual subspace is bijective

nodes.summary: The wandering subspace of an isometry `V`: the orthogonal complement of its range. Vectors here are orthogonal to every vector in the range of `V`.
nodes.title: Wandering subspace of an isometry

nodes.summary: Uniqueness of the Wold decomposition at level `n`: the remainder and the finite wandering sum are uniquely determined.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the finite Wold decomposition

nodes.summary: Pythagoras for a Wold decomposition: the squared norm of a vector is the sum of the squared norms of its wandering coefficients plus the squared norm of the remainder.
nodes.title: Pythagorean identity for the Wold decomposition

nodes.summary: Applying the residual unitary is the same as applying `V` and viewing the result in the ambient space.
nodes.title: Action of the residual unitary of an isometry

nodes.summary: The isometry restricts to a unitary operator (a linear isometric equivalence) on its residual subspace.
nodes.title: Unitary part of an isometry on its residual subspace

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
